label: Linden Row Partners — Independent Review of the Harbour Programme
covers: An external reviewer's report about somebody else's programme, which must put NOTHING in a grid column and must still hand back everything it printed, in unmapped. The two documents already in the set that cover this shape expect nothing anywhere, so their recall is a free 1 and a run that returns an empty extraction scores a clean sheet on them. This one expects every paragraph in unmapped, so losing the content is lost recall. The failure this catches is a quiet drop in recall on exactly the documents whose whole content lives in unmapped, which is on record from a real review document and was invisible to this benchmark.

slides.title: Linden Row Partners — Independent Review of the Harbour Programme

columns.heading: SCOPE OF THIS REVIEW
items: Linden Row Partners was commissioned in March to review the Harbour Programme's second delivery year and to report to the funding board.
The review drew on the programme's own monitoring returns, two unannounced site visits and conversations with nine staff and fourteen participants.
No comparison group was available, so this review does not attempt to attribute change to the programme.

columns.heading: WHAT WE OBSERVED
items: Delivery ran in all four harbour-side neighbourhoods, with the Thursday cohort moving venue twice during the year.
Staffing was thin in the autumn term, when two of the five keyworker posts sat vacant for nine weeks.
Participants we spoke to described the keyworker relationship as the thing they would miss if the programme ended.

columns.heading: WHERE THE EVIDENCE IS WEAK
items: Attendance is recorded three different ways across the four sites, so the headline figure in the annual return cannot be reconciled.
The confidence measure used at intake was written in-house and has not been validated against anything.
Outcomes for the participants who left before week six are not recorded at all, and they are a fifth of the intake.

columns.heading: RECOMMENDATIONS TO THE BOARD
items: Agree one attendance definition across the four sites before the third delivery year opens.
Commission an independent assessment of the confidence measure, or replace it with a validated instrument.
Record a leaving reason for every participant who stops attending, however briefly they were enrolled.
